issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Refactor DeletePost Endpoint for Database Transaction Atomicity and Query Optimization

  • Date: 2026-10-21
  • Status: Completed
  • Coverage: 100% PASS

1. Summary

Refactored src/Action/V1/Posts/DeletePost.go to eliminate SQL Cartesian products, guarantee database transaction atomicity, and optimize storage client handling:

  1. Targeted Query Architecture:

    • Replaced the monolithic 5-join query with targeted indexed lookups.
    • Removed ~80 lines of manual linear deduplication loops.
    • Initial post check fails fast with HTTP 409 Conflict if not found or unauthorized.

  2. Atomic Database Transaction:

    • Wrapped deletions of bucket_containers, notifications, posts, and empty collection_post records in Config.DB.Transaction.
    • Single batch query for bucket_containers deletion (key IN ?).
    • If any deletion fails, all database changes roll back cleanly.

  3. Storage & Downstream Optimization:

    • Initialized MinioFunctions.InitMinioClient() once and reused across file deletion loops.
    • Preserved all downstream synchronizations (SyncPostWithMapsPanorra, AddCounterTotalPosts, Elasticsearch reply comment/bookmark containers, Redis invalidation).

  4. Automated Unit Testing:

    • Created src/Action/V1/Posts/DeletePost_test.go with TestShouldDeletePostFile and TestDeletePost_UnauthorizedWhenUserDataFails.

1. Problem & Context

The DELETE /posts/:sid endpoint (src/Action/V1/Posts/DeletePost.go) exhibited severe architectural and performance bottlenecks:

  1. Cartesian Product Query:
    • The query used a single raw SQL query with 5 simultaneous LEFT JOIN clauses (comment, users, collection_post, bookmark, folder_bookmark, and multiple_post).
    • For posts with multiple comments, bookmarks, and collection posts, this generated a Cartesian product with thousands of duplicate rows in memory, requiring over 80 lines of manual linear search loops to deduplicate IDs.
  2. Lack of Database Transaction (ACID Violation):
    • Sequential deletions across bucket_containers, notifications, posts, and collection_post_detail were performed without a transaction.
    • Any failure or network timeout during the process resulted in partial deletion and orphaned records in the database.
  3. Repeated Client Initialization:
    • In multiplePost handling, MinioFunctions.InitMinioClient() was called repeatedly inside the loop for every file path.

2. Scope

  1. Eliminate Cartesian Product Query:

    • Fetch the targeted post first using standard GORM model query (Where(qSid, sid).Where("user_id = ?", userId).First(&post)). If missing, return HTTP 409 Conflict immediately.
    • Fetch related identifiers (commentIDs, multiPostPaths, bookmarkInfos, collectionPostIDs) via separate, targeted indexed queries without Cartesian products or manual deduplication loops.

  2. Atomic Database Transaction:

    • Wrap all mutating database operations in Config.DB.Transaction(func(tx *gorm.DB) error { ... }):
      • Batch deletion of bucket_containers.
      • Deletion of notifications for the post.
      • Deletion of the posts record.
      • Cleanup of empty collection_post records.

  3. Storage & Downstream Optimization:

    • Initialize MinIO client once before file deletion loops.
    • Perform downstream Elasticsearch indexing and Redis cache updates only after the database transaction successfully commits.

  4. Automated Unit Testing:

    • Create src/Action/V1/Posts/DeletePost_test.go testing shouldDeletePostFile across environments and unauthorized access rejections.

3. Behavior Boundary

  • 100% Backward Compatible:
    • Route /delete/:sid, query parameter pw, encryption envelopes (sl=true, ec=true), HTTP status codes, and JSON response bodies remain identical.
    • S3/MinIO bucket file deletion, local file removal, and downstream Elasticsearch/Redis triggers remain identical.

4. Acceptance Criteria

  • Cartesian product query and manual deduplication loops eliminated.
  • Database mutations are fully atomic inside Config.DB.Transaction.
  • All unit tests pass cleanly (go test ./src/Action/V1/Posts/...).
  • Project builds cleanly (go build ./cmd/...).
